previous.passage: When the buffet doors opened, the wedding hall in Busan dissolved into a hundred conversations, and Sunja let the noise carry her to a corner table. Joon, her grandson, slid in beside her, tugging at a collar his mother had ironed too stiffly. He was laughing about the cousin who had tripped on the aisle runner, and Sunja laughed too, swatting his wrist for being unkind. Then he drew a creased photograph from his jacket: a young woman in a borrowed hanbok, standing beside a man no one in the family had ever named. Sunja's hand stopped above her plate. Around them the hall went on clapping for the couple, but at the corner table the air had thinned. She studied the face she had once worn and did not reach for the picture. Joon, sensing he had opened something he could not close, set his chopsticks down without a sound. Somewhere a microphone squealed, and the master of ceremonies announced the cake.
previous.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From nostalgic reverence for a wedding custom to open resentment toward the relatives who arranged it
From anxious uncertainty about a family gathering to relieved delight once a missing relative is identified
From formal politeness between near strangers to warm familiarity after the two discover a shared memory
From playful teasing between relatives to a hushed unease after an unexplained image is revealed
previous.explanation: 앞부분에서 Joon과 Sunja는 넘어진 사촌 이야기로 함께 웃고 손목을 치며 장난스럽게 대화한다. 사진이 나온 뒤 Sunja의 손이 멈추고 '공기가 희박해졌다', Joon이 소리 없이 젓가락을 내려놓는 등 조용하고 불편한 분위기로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 결혼 관습에 대한 경외나 원망이 없고, B는 사진 속 남자가 끝내 밝혀지지 않으며, C는 두 사람이 처음부터 가까운 가족이라 맞지 않다.

previous.passage: Who goes to the cinema in Tromso in May, when the sun refuses to set and no one needs the dark? Anders asked himself this as he bought a ticket from a girl reading a magazine. Inside, the theater held eleven people, and one of them was Anneke, who had not come to Mass in three years. She waved with the cheerful ease of someone meeting her dentist at a party, and Anders sat two seats away, pleased by the coincidence. They traded jokes about the stale popcorn. Then Anneke's daughter leaned across her mother's lap. "Why don't we go to church anymore?" she asked. "You said it was because Father Anders moved away." Anneke looked at the blank screen. Anders looked at his ticket stub, folding it into smaller and smaller squares, and neither of them answered. When the lights finally dimmed, both seemed grateful for the advertisements.
previous.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It shifts from lighthearted banter between two acquaintances to strained silence once a child exposes an excuse.
It shifts from quiet suspicion between a priest and a parishioner to open reconciliation prompted by a child.

It shifts from solemn reflection on the northern summer to cheerful anticipation of the film about to begin.
previous.explanation: 처음에 Anneke는 쾌활하게 손을 흔들고 두 사람은 눅눅한 팝콘에 대해 농담을 주고받는다. 그러나 딸이 신부가 이사 갔다는 엄마의 핑계를 드러내자 두 사람은 대답하지 못하고 화면과 표만 바라보는 어색한 침묵에 빠진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 화해가 일어나지 않고, C는 설교에 대한 오해가 아니며, D는 광고를 반기는 것이 기대가 아니라 침묵에서 벗어난 안도이므로 틀리다.

previous.passage: Kagiso never hurried at the post office. He stood at the counter with his hat in his hands while the clerk weighed a parcel of seed catalogs, and he answered every question about the rain twice. Marcus, the surveyor from Cape Town, stood behind him checking his watch, a loan document under his arm that needed the farmer's signature before the afternoon bus. At first Marcus tapped the paper against his leg. Then the clerk mentioned that Kagiso's late wife had once run this counter, and that the old scale was hers. Marcus stopped tapping. He looked at the brass weights, worn smooth at the handles, and at the farmer's careful fingers, and he thought of the six-month extension his office liked to call a favor. When Kagiso finally turned around, Marcus found himself asking about the rain. Outside, the bus driver honked once and pulled away down the gravel road.
previous.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a man's impatience with a slow errand, then traces how a revealed detail alters his outlook.
It describes a farmer's financial troubles, then explains the legal terms of the loan he is offered.
It recounts a dispute at a post office, then shows how the clerk settles it in the farmer's favor.
It contrasts life in the city with life on a farm, then argues that rural customs are worth preserving.
previous.explanation: 지문은 시계를 보며 서류로 다리를 두드리는 Marcus의 조급함으로 시작한다. 이후 저울이 Kagiso의 죽은 아내 것이었다는 사실이 드러나자 Marcus는 두드리기를 멈추고, 대출 연장을 다시 생각하며 결국 자신도 비 이야기를 묻는다. 따라서 조급함을 제시한 뒤 드러난 세부 사실이 시각을 바꾸는 과정을 따라간다는 A가 정답이다. B의 법적 조건 설명, C의 분쟁 해결, D의 주장은 지문에 없다.

previous.passage: Bao did not like surprises. As captain of the river freighter, he had found Wira curled among the rice sacks two days out, and now, docked below the terraced hills outside Hanoi, he had brought the boy home to eat because there was nowhere else to put him. Bao's mother set out bowls and chopsticks. Wira, from an island far to the south, hesitated, then began eating with his right hand as his family always had. Bao's mother watched a moment, then set down her own chopsticks and tore a piece of rice cake with her fingers. Bao felt the meal tilt on its hinge, the old customs of his house swinging open to make room for another. By the end, neither of them was eating the way they had begun, and no one remarked on it. Mist gathered over the terraces, erasing the lower paddies one by one.
previous.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the meal tilt on its hinge” most nearly suggests
options: a moment of clumsiness that nearly overturned the dishes on the table.
a sudden decision by Bao to send the boy away from his mother's house.

previous.explanation: 문 경첩이 돌듯 식사가 기울었다는 표현 바로 뒤에 집안의 오랜 관습이 열리며 다른 관습을 위한 자리를 만든다는 설명이 이어진다. 또한 Bao의 어머니가 젓가락을 내려놓고 손으로 먹기 시작하고, 끝에는 아무도 처음 방식대로 먹지 않는다. 따라서 이 비유는 집안의 관습이 손님의 습관을 받아들이는 변화를 뜻하므로 정답은 C이다. A는 경첩을 물리적 사고로 읽었고, B와 D는 지문의 행동과 반대 방향이다.

previous.passage: Dakar's Corniche was nearly empty at dusk when Yuto and Kwesi locked the shutters of their radio-repair shop for what might be the last time. Their oldest friend lay in the hospital above the promenade, and he believed the shop was thriving; they had told him so at every visit, describing customers who did not exist. Kwesi wanted to keep the story going a little longer. Yuto walked beside him along the sea wall and said nothing for a long while. He had begun to feel that their kindness had become a lantern without oil, something they kept holding up long after it had stopped giving any light. At the hospital stairs he stopped. He would tell their friend the truth, he said, and then they would sit with him for as long as visiting hours allowed. Kwesi looked at the sea before nodding. Fishermen were hauling their painted pirogues up the wet sand.
previous.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a lantern without oil” most nearly suggests
options: a costly gift that the brothers could no longer afford to give.
a secret that the dying friend had long been hiding from them.
a failing shop that needed repairs before it could reopen.
a comfort still offered though it no longer helped anyone.
previous.explanation: 형제는 친구에게 가게가 잘된다는 거짓 이야기를 계속 들려주었고, Yuto는 그 친절이 더는 빛을 내지 못하는데도 계속 들고 있는 등불 같다고 느낀다. 이어서 그는 진실을 말하기로 결심하므로, 이 비유는 이미 효과를 잃은 위로를 가리킨다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 비용 문제로, B는 친구의 비밀로 잘못 읽었고, C는 가게라는 소재를 쓰지만 비유의 대상이 아니다.

previous.passage: Dario hung his uniforms on the rooftop line every morning at six, after our night shift at the bakery in Oaxaca, and I, Tendai, hung mine beside his. For months he had talked of quitting to drive a taxi with his cousin; he kept the license forms folded in his wallet and showed them to anyone who asked. That spring he spoke of it less. One morning I noticed he had begun pinning a second apron to the line, the white one the head baker gave only to those training for the ovens. He did not mention it, and neither did I. When I finally asked about the taxi, he shrugged and said his plans had gone out with the wash, faded a little each time until he could no longer remember their color. Below us the street vendors were unfolding their umbrellas, one stripe at a time.

he had deliberately thrown away the taxi forms he once carried.

previous.passage: "Careful, that bow is older than both of us," Gunnar said, grinning, as Callum fumbled it beside the cafe's sugar bowl. Trains hissed beyond the Rotterdam windows, and the conductor teased the boy about his cold coffee and his crooked collar. Callum asked whose bow it had been. Gunnar's grin faded. He turned the bow slowly in his hands, thumb resting on the worn grip where another thumb had worn it first. He said that his teacher had played with it for forty years and had left it to him without a note. For a while he only watched the departures board. Then he set the bow in front of Callum and pushed it gently across the table.

previous.passage: When I was nineteen, my stepfather and I worked the dark hours at Rivka's bakery in Haifa, shaping dough before the shutters rose. He had paid my first year of tuition with money meant for his own retirement, and neither of us ever spoke of it. For months I treated those mornings as a chore, sulking over the cold flour and his habit of humming off-key. Then one morning Rivka mentioned, offhand, that he had taken extra shifts all winter. I watched him fold the challah with his cracked knuckles and felt my impatience drain into something closer to awe. I began arriving early to light the ovens before he came. He never asked why, and I never explained.

당신은 디지털 SAT Reading & Writing 문학 지문 문항 출제 위원이다. 아래 10개 후보 각각에 대해 문항 1개를 만들어 JSON 한 파일로 저장한다.

규칙:

2. 지문·질문·선택지는 영어만 쓴다. 해설(explanation)만 한국어 3~5문장이며, 글자 참조는 선택지 글자(A~D)로만 한다.

4. 선택지 길이·문체를 비슷하게 맞춘다. 정답이 가장 길거나 구체적이면 탈락한다. 오답 3개는 서로 다른 그럴듯한 오개념에서 나오게 하고 지문 표현을 일부 활용한다.
5. 정답이 지문 마지막 문장을 거의 그대로 바꿔 말한 것이면 탈락한다. 근거를 서로 떨어진 둘 이상의 문장에 둔다.
6. 후보별 names 에 있는 이름만 인물 이름으로 쓴다. 지정되지 않은 이름·'Tobias'·'Odalys'·'Wren' 은 쓰지 않는다. 후보별 openingStyle 을 따르고 첫 단어를 The·You·It·There 로 시작하지 않는다.
